macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global markets mostly cautious ahead of Nvidia earnings and U.S. inflation data
items.summary: Asian equities were mixed to firmer as investors waited for Nvidia’s results and key U.S. inflation readings, with traders treating the combination as a major test for the AI trade and the Federal Reserve outlook. U.S. equity futures were slightly weaker, including Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.3% and S&P 500 futures down 0.1%.

items.title: Oil prices fall as Middle East tensions ease, easing bond-yield pressure
items.summary: Brent crude extended its decline, falling about 1.7% to around $87 a barrel, after reports that Iran and Oman discussed an interim framework to resume shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Lower oil prices were also seen as reducing inflation pressure and supporting bonds.

items.title: U.S. PCE inflation data due, keeping Fed policy expectations in focus
items.summary: Markets were waiting for the U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, for clues on the next policy move. Traders were also watching remarks expected around Jackson Hole, which could influence rate-cut expectations.

items.title: Dollar steady as investors await inflation reports and Jackson Hole
items.summary: The U.S. dollar traded in a narrow range in early Asian hours as currency markets stayed on hold ahead of major inflation releases and the Jackson Hole symposium. The Reuters report said investors were awaiting inflation readings from major economies, including the U.S.

items.title: Gold near three-month high ahead of U.S. inflation data and Fed signals
items.summary: Gold was little changed to slightly lower but remained near a three-month high as investors awaited the U.S. PCE report and a major Jackson Hole speech tied to the Fed outlook. The report said traders were pricing in a 60.4% chance the Fed would leave rates unchanged next month.

items.title: Canada retaliates with tariffs on more than 700 U.S. products
items.summary: Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on more than 700 products, escalating the trade dispute with the U.S. The move was described as matching Washington’s latest duties dollar-for-dollar.

items.title: Indian benchmarks rise despite global caution
items.summary: India’s Nifty 50 closed up 0.48% at 24,334.55 and the Sensex gained 286.98 points to 77,656.09. The move came even as global markets remained focused on Nvidia earnings, U.S. inflation data, and oil-price declines.

items.title: U.S. Treasury yields fall as markets await key data
items.summary: U.S. Treasury yields declined while the dollar stayed steady, reflecting a wait-and-see mood before major inflation releases and Jackson Hole. The market backdrop was shaped by softer oil prices and caution over the Fed path.

items.title: Chinese and Japanese policy backdrop remains active
items.summary: A market recap highlighted the Bank of Japan’s planned Jackson Hole representation, alongside stronger-than-expected Japanese producer service inflation and Chinese liquidity operations. The same report noted a firmer yuan and PBOC open-market repos to inject liquidity.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly topped $81K before slipping back below $79K
items.summary: Bitcoin rose above $80,000 and reached as high as about $81,200 in the past 24 hours, then retreated to around $78,900 as the broader crypto market pulled back. Ether, XRP, SOL, and DOGE also fell, with several major tokens down roughly 1% to 5% over the day.

items.title: Crypto rally tied to Treasury buyback plans, ETF inflows, and short covering
items.summary: Market reports linked Bitcoin’s surge to U.S. Treasury bond buyback plans, strong exchange-traded fund inflows, and heavy short covering in derivatives markets. One report said the rally also reflected renewed flows into crypto amid concerns about U.S. fiscal health and dollar weakness.

items.title: Trump-backed CLARITY Act push cited as crypto price catalyst
items.summary: A market report said President Donald Trump’s push for Congress to approve the long-awaited CLARITY Act helped support the latest crypto rally. The same report noted that Bitcoin, Ether, and XRP all gave back some of their earlier gains after the move above $80,000.

items.title: Bitcoin and major altcoins under pressure after short-term spike
items.summary: Several reports described a broad crypto pullback, with Bitcoin near $78,400 to $78,800, Ether around $2,430 to $2,456, XRP near $1.43 to $1.47, and Solana near $96 to $97. Total crypto market capitalization also eased from recent highs, signaling profit-taking after the surge.

items.title: Solana outperforms Bitcoin as ETF inflows fuel rally
items.summary: Solana was highlighted as outperforming Bitcoin, with one report saying record ETF inflows helped drive SOL toward the $100 level. The report said SOL traded around $98 while Bitcoin was slightly lower on the day.

items.title: Crypto market posts a mild correction; BNB, SOL, and ZEC fall
items.summary: A market update said Bitcoin briefly slipped below $78,000 before recovering to around $78,500, while Ether held near $2,443. Solana fell back after crossing $100, BNB dropped below $700, and ZEC declined nearly 7% over 24 hours.

items.title: Altcoin winners and losers stand out in overnight trading
items.summary: One market feed reported strong 24-hour gains in smaller tokens such as BMT, ONG, and PROM, while PEOPLE, STORJ, and MUBARAK suffered losses near 20%. It also noted sharply lower trading in several mid-cap names including JTO, ETHFI, DASH, and MET.

items.title: No major regulatory announcement beyond the CLARITY Act push was identified in the provided results
items.summary: The search results included only one notable policy angle: renewed attention to the U.S. CLARITY Act, which was cited as a supportive factor for crypto prices. No other clearly sourced, major regulatory development from the past 24 hours appeared in the supplied material.

items.title: Notable project developments: Zcash ETF launch and digital-ruble adoption
items.summary: One result said Zcash hit an eight-year high as the world’s first ZEC ETF went live, marking a notable project-level development. Another reported that Russian telecom and e-commerce firms will begin accepting the digital ruble from September, signaling wider CBDC adoption.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Taiwan indicts nine over alleged illegal export of AI servers to China
items.summary: Taiwanese prosecutors charged nine people, including an Nvidia employee and two Super Micro employees, in a case involving alleged illegal exports of high-end AI servers to China. The case highlights tightening enforcement around advanced AI hardware supply chains.

items.title: Apple unveils faster Mac mini and Mac Studio for AI workloads
items.summary: Apple announced new Mac mini and Mac Studio systems aimed at AI use cases, with the Mac mini described as offering up to 4x faster AI performance. Reuters said the launch was part of Apple’s push to capitalize on the AI boom.

items.title: Nvidia unveils Jetson Orin Nano 2 edge AI computer
items.summary: Nvidia introduced the Jetson Orin Nano 2, an edge AI computer it says doubles inference performance and delivers 78 TOPS of AI compute. The announcement adds to ongoing competition in compact AI hardware.

items.title: Murf AI launches Falcon 2 text-to-speech model
items.summary: Murf AI said it has launched Falcon 2, a text-to-speech model focused on more human-like voices at lower cost and faster speed. The release reflects continued product momentum in voice AI.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly slows model development after security setback
items.summary: Last week, IPO-bound OpenAI said it would slow the pace of model development while overhauling research and training systems after officials were caught off guard by an AI agent testing incident involving Hugging Face. The move underscores growing concern about agent security and operational risk.

items.title: IBM Research announces Granite 4.2 model family
items.summary: IBM Research released Granite 4.2, a model family focused on agentic reasoning and speech, with 3B, 8B, and 30B parameter variants. The models were published on Hugging Face.

items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini Enterprise for Legal and Financial Services
items.summary: Google Cloud formally introduced Gemini Enterprise for Legal and Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services. The launches point to a broader trend toward verticalized enterprise AI products.

items.title: Japan adopts guideline asking AI providers to disclose training data and methods
items.summary: Japan’s government approved a policy asking domestic and overseas AI providers to disclose summaries of their training data and training methods. The measure is non-binding for now but signals tighter scrutiny of foundation-model development.

items.title: OpenAI’s Assistants API reaches formal end of life
items.summary: Developers were warned that OpenAI’s Assistants API is being formally discontinued. The change is likely to force application migrations and reprioritize OpenAI’s developer platform.

items.title: Thomson Reuters launches its first in-house AI model
items.summary: Thomson Reuters said it has released Thomson, its first proprietary large language model. The launch signals growing pressure on information-services firms to build their own AI systems.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Gamescom ONL spotlights major reveals, including The Witcher 3 remaster and FF7 updates
items.summary: Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 delivered several major announcements, including a remastered version of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, new Final Fantasy VII content, and multiple fresh trailers and release-date updates across big franchises. Coverage from live recap articles highlights this as the biggest gaming news event in the last 24 hours.

items.title: CD Projekt Red announces The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered
items.summary: The Witcher 3 remaster was revealed with visual and gameplay improvements, plus free access to the Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine expansions for base-game owners. The update is scheduled for September 29, according to event coverage.

items.title: HoYoverse unveils new game Nodus Fall at Gamescom
items.summary: HoYoverse introduced a new project called Nodus Fall during Opening Night Live, making it one of the event's most notable surprise announcements. Multiple recap outlets singled it out as a headline reveal from the showcase.

items.title: Path of Exile 2 confirms 1.0 release date
items.summary: Grinding Gear Games announced that Path of Exile 2 will leave early access and launch as version 1.0 on December 11, 2026. Coverage notes that the release will also bring the game to a broader audience as it exits its current testing phase.

items.title: AION 2 gets worldwide release date
items.summary: NCSoft confirmed that AION 2 will launch globally on October 5, with Gamescom coverage noting the MMORPG's shift from a regional rollout to a worldwide release. The announcement was among the most prominent industry-date updates from ONL.

items.title: Saber Interactive delays Turok: Origins to spring 2027
items.summary: Saber Interactive said Turok: Origins will no longer launch this fall and is now slated for spring 2027. The game remains planned for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day shows new story trailer
items.summary: Gamescom coverage says the latest Gears of War: E-Day trailer focused on story and drama while revealing key plot elements, including a Locust leader. The reveal kept the game high on the list of talked-about upcoming releases.

items.title: Esports and industry pressure continue to shape Gamescom coverage
items.summary: Broader Gamescom reporting emphasized that the industry is still dealing with layoffs and intense competition, with one report citing nearly 10,000 gaming job losses since January and a projected 15,000 layoffs this year. That context framed the event as both a celebration and a business reset point.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: SpaceX plans $100 billion Starship launch complex in Louisiana
items.summary: SpaceX unveiled plans to build a new Starship rocket launch complex in southern Louisiana, a major expansion tied to the company’s future launch operations. The project would reportedly transform coastal wetlands into a key base for SpaceX’s ambitions.

items.title: Tesla recalls nearly 3 million vehicles in China over door-handle safety risks
items.summary: Tesla is recalling about 2.98 million vehicles in China, including Model 3, Y, X and S vehicles, over door-handle safety concerns. The recall is part of a broader wave of vehicle safety actions affecting millions of cars in China.

items.title: Brazil fines ByteDance nearly $30 million over children’s data handling
items.summary: Brazil’s data protection regulator fined TikTok parent ByteDance more than 153 million reais, or nearly $30 million, over alleged failures in handling personal data for children and teenagers. The case adds to regulatory pressure on major platforms over privacy and safety compliance.

items.title: TikTok settles U.S. children’s privacy lawsuit for $400 million
items.summary: TikTok reached a $400 million settlement with the U.S. Department of Justice, ending a 2024 lawsuit over alleged violations of federal children’s privacy laws. The agreement includes an immediate payment and a later payment after a prior consent decree is vacated.

items.title: Dutch regulators fine Uber nearly $1 billion over driver account suspensions
items.summary: Dutch data protection authorities fined Uber nearly $1 billion, saying the company used automated systems to suspend driver accounts without human review in some cases. The penalty is one of the largest privacy-related fines reported in the past day.

items.title: Australia bars fully AI-generated songs from official music charts
items.summary: Australia’s recorded music industry said tracks wholly generated by AI will be excluded from official charts. The policy responds to concerns that synthetic music could undercut artists’ livelihoods and distort chart rankings.

items.title: Taiwan charges nine people over illegal export of high-end server hardware to China
items.summary: Taiwanese prosecutors charged nine people, including employees linked to Nvidia and Super Micro, in a case involving the alleged illegal export of high-end servers to China. The case highlights continued scrutiny of semiconductor and server supply chains.

items.title: Chinese humanoid robot sets 100-meter sprint record in Beijing
items.summary: A Chinese humanoid robot set a new 100-meter sprint record of 8.86 seconds at a robotics event in Beijing. The achievement underscores rapid progress in robotics hardware and mobility performance.

items.title: Airtel Africa and Starlink launch satellite-to-mobile service in the Democratic Republic of Congo
items.summary: Airtel Africa and Starlink launched satellite-to-mobile service in the Democratic Republic of Congo, which the operator says is the first commercial launch of Starlink’s satellite connectivity service in the country. The rollout expands low-infrastructure connectivity options in a major African market.

items.title: SpaceX’s Starlink 10-49 mission set to mark Falcon 9’s 100th launch of 2026
items.summary: SpaceX’s Starlink 10-49 mission is expected to become the 100th Falcon 9 launch of 2026. The milestone reflects the company’s unusually high launch cadence this year.
